idee.titre: The verb agrees with the head noun

etapes.texte: The TOEIC hides the subject **far from the verb**

ex1.titre: Cross out the words in the middle

bulles.texte: The **list** __of new items__ **is** on your desk.

speciaux.titre: They look plural, but they are singular

q.lu: The **results** of the customer survey ------- very positive.

etapes.texte: Find the **head noun**, at the start of the subject
Cross out **of ..., in ..., with ...** between subject and verb

phrases.texte: The rule is simple. A singular subject takes a singular verb. A plural subject takes a plural verb.
But the TOEIC hides the subject far from the verb.
The list of new items is on your desk. The subject is list, not items. So the verb is singular.
phrases.dit: The list of new items is on your desk. The subject is list, not items. So the verb is singular.

phrases.texte: The managers in the Paris office are busy. The subject is managers. So the verb is plural.
Some subjects look plural, but they are singular. Each and every: each employee has a badge.
phrases.dit: Some subjects look plural, but they are singular. Each, and every: each employee has a badge.

phrases.texte: Everyone and nobody: everyone is ready. And news and information: the information is correct.
phrases.dit: Everyone, and nobody: everyone is ready. And news, and information: the information is correct.

phrases.texte: Now, a TOEIC question. The results of the customer survey, blank, very positive.
A: is. B: are. C: was. D: being.
phrases.dit: Answer A. is. Answer B. are. Answer C. was. Answer D. being.

phrases.texte: The word just before the blank is survey, singular. That is the trap. The real subject is results.
Results is plural. So is and was are wrong. And being is not a full verb.
phrases.dit: Results is plural. So, is, and was, are wrong. And being, is not a full verb.

phrases.texte: B is correct: the results of the customer survey are very positive.
Three steps. One: find the head noun, at the start of the subject.
Two: cross out the words between the subject and the verb.
Three: each, every, everyone and information are always singular.
Now practise with the questions below.
phrases.dit: Now, practise with the questions below.
